lessons.title: -mente — with no upper limit
lessons.gloss: the ending with no upper limit — and it is a noun for "mind" that stopped being one

segments.text: Two endings so far, and each was worth a fixed number of words. This one has no number, because you can make it yourself.
rápidamente becomes rapidly, claramente becomes clearly, perfectamente becomes perfectly, naturalmente becomes naturally.
And unlike the last two endings, this one is a machine rather than a list: take an adjective, put it in its feminine form, add -mente.
rápido becomes rápida becomes rápidamente claro becomes clara becomes claramente.

That feminine step looks arbitrary and is not — the next section says why. But the practical effect is that every adjective you ever learn comes with a free adverb, which is why this ending has no count attached. Its reach is however many adjectives you end up knowing.
-mente is not an ending at all, historically. It is the Latin noun mente, "with a mind" — and mente is feminine, which is the whole explanation for that feminine adjective.

Latin said clārā mente, "with a clear mind," and the adjective agreed with the noun because that is what adjectives do. Then the phrase fused, the noun stopped being a noun, and the agreement was left behind as a rule nobody could explain any more.
So rápidamente is, at the bottom, "with a rapid mind." Every Spanish adverb in -mente is quietly a phrase about somebody's state of mind.
English does exactly the same thing with a different body part. -ly is Old English -līce, from līc, "body, form" — so clearly is "in a clear form." Two languages, two fused nouns, the same idea.

segments.prompt: Why does the adjective go feminine before -mente?
acceptedResponses: because mente is a feminine noun
it used to agree with the noun mente

feedback.correct: Agreement left behind after the noun stopped being one.
feedback.incorrect: Mente is a feminine noun, and the adjective was agreeing with it.

feedback.correct: Every -mente adverb is secretly about a state of mind.

segments.text: English -ly becomes? (-mente.) What do you do to the adjective first? (Make it feminine.) And why? (Because mente was a feminine noun meaning mind.) Next: the three of them together.
